spĕcŭlābundus , a, um, adj. id.,
I.on the look-out, on the watch; watching for any thing (post-Aug.): “Festus Hadrumeto, ubi speculabundus substiterat, etc.,” Tac. H. 4, 50 : “ab ostio speculabunda,” Mart. Cap. 2, § 112 .—With acc.: “speculabundus ex altissimā rupe identidem signa,” Suet. Tib. 65 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
